_header: SEAL PREDICATE — NEGATIVE CONTROL. Feeding this to `node tooling/grip/seal.mjs --ledger` must exit 1
and must name ALL FOUR clauses as failing, SEPARATELY. Read the clean twin's header first: under
--ledger nothing live is read, so this proves only that the command is ABLE TO FAIL.
It breaks each clause by a DIFFERENT mechanism, so a fix that silently collapses two clauses into
(a)  criterion 0 declares an ABSENCE polarity over a `diff` that exits 1 WITH content attached.
That reads FAILED — exactly like an honest zero-match grep — but carries absenceEligible
false, so admitsAbsenceClaim vetoes it. This is the D109 softening made executable: a seal
that 'just accepts FAILED' goes GREEN on this row while accepting a multi-kilobyte diff as
proof that something is not there. Criterion 1 declares no polarity at all and fails closed.
(b)  two namespace rows are claimable, and ONE OF THEM (tgw2-verify-writes-back) is invisible to
the prior art's filter[parent_id] lens because it hangs at depth 2 under a done parent. A
port that kept fetchRoster reports one fewer blocking row than exists.
(b') the ROOT IS ABSENT FROM THE POOL. This is the clause D108 warns is deleted by inheritance:
the prior art excludes its root by construction, never by a check, so there is nothing to
fail. Here there is, and it fails on POOL MEMBERSHIP alone — a (b') keyed on `claim == null`
or on the root's own status would pass this row and the amendment would be vacuous.
(c)  the root document is already `done`: the seal is being asked to bless an out-of-order close

criteria.criterion: an absence claim resting on a diff that exited 1 with content — the D50 veto must fire

criteria.why: no declared polarity — fails closed even though the command itself is ADMITTED at L2
